chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Suleyman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding the blood money (diyah) of the murdered that the inheritors inherit it according to the Book of Allah and their shares, if there is no debt upon the murdered, except for the brothers and sisters from the mother, for they do not inherit anything from his blood money.

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for murder/manslaughter

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the blood money of a murdered person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the blood money (diyah) of a murder victim is distributed according to standard inheritance shares, yet it introduces a specific jurisprudential exception where maternal siblings are excluded from receiving any portion. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of maternal kin in Shia inheritance law, distinguishing them from full and paternal siblings who typically share in such compensations. The narration underscores the precision of Imam Ali’s judicial application of Quranic principles to specific financial liabilities.
